column1: # xbios-flush-r1.tsv -- DUMPBIOS, the keyboard flush io->ibufhd = io->ibuftl
# through Iorec(1)'s pointer WITH KEYS IN THE RING (TASK/XBIOS01, acceptance
# docs/analysis/ORACLE.md).  xbios-ptr-r1.tsv's flush ran on an empty ring:
# it shows only that the write is taken.  Here three keys (a, b, c) are in
# the IKBD ring before the flush, and Bconstat(2) must say so (-1) and then 0.
# NOT a plain table run: the keys come from outside the dumper.  Oracle:
# dumper's LOG says "running N cases", --fast-forward off (real-time VBLs);
# NewTOS: the scratch IKBD injector (tools/inject-arm.py, launch:DUMPBIOS),
# which feeds at a trap-side input pump -- here the Bconstat(2) calls.  Method
# Bconin(2) waits for input and is refused by the loader, so the Vsync run
# below is the wait: about 3 s of frames for the Hatari keys to arrive.  The
# precondition case (Bconstat(2) = -1, Iorec(1) head 0 / tail 12) proves the
# keys were there; a run where they were not shows it as a difference.
# Frozen once measured (the CRC of this file is in the dump header).
# ---- the ring before any key: empty (bios/ikbd.c:242-246); on NewTOS this pump arms the injector
# ---- the wait: three keys a, b, c arrive (Hatari fifo; NewTOS injector at the next pump)

column5: Bconstat(2): NewTOS input pump, the injector feeds the keys here
Bconstat(2): a second pump (an injector armed only at the first)
Bconstat(2) = -1: keys in the ring before the flush -- bios/ikbd.c:242-246
Iorec(1) before the flush: head 0, tail 12 (three 4-byte entries) -- bios/ikbd.c:157-173
Iorec(1) after the flush: head == tail == 12
